problem_motivation.content: The poor oxidation resistance of RHEAs is a major obstacle preventing their use in high-temperature engineering applications.
problem_motivation.evidence_span: However, the poor oxidation resistance of RHEAs is a major obstacle for their use in high-temperature engineering applications, as are RMs.

prior_approach.content: Previous studies have reported the use of silicide coatings, such as Si-20Cr-20Fe, to protect refractory metals and alloys.
prior_approach.evidence_span: Among anti-oxidation coatings, silicide coatings have been widely used to protect RMs and many studies have addressed on the Si-20Cr-20Fe coating.

prior_approach.content: Gorr et al. reported on equiatomic AlCrMoTi-X RHEAs and demonstrated improved oxidation resistance compared to other materials.
prior_approach.evidence_span: Gorr et al. reported two equiatomic AlCrMoTi-X (X = Nb or Ta) RHEAs [ [18] , [24] ].

prior_approach.content: Sankar et al. analyzed the microstructure and composition evolution of the Si-20Cr-20Fe coating on C103 alloy to explain its mechanisms.
prior_approach.evidence_span: Sankar et al. analyzed the microstructure and composition evolution of the Si-20Cr-20Fe coating on C103 alloy during oxidation and explained the formation and oxidation resistance mechanisms of the silicide coating [ [30] ].

prior_approach.content: Previous studies on niobium and tantalum alloys show silicide coatings typically have outer disilicide and inner low silicide layers.
prior_approach.evidence_span: Previous investigations of silicide coatings on niobium alloys and tantalum alloys have shown that the outermost layers of the silicide coatings are disilicide layers, and the inner layers are low silicide layers

prior_limitation.content: RHEAs are susceptible to oxidation in high-temperature environments, necessitating protection.
prior_limitation.evidence_span: protecting RHEAs from oxidation at high-temperature environments

prior_limitation.content: Adding anti-oxidant alloy elements to improve oxidation resistance inevitably diminishes the mechanical properties of the alloys.
prior_limitation.evidence_span: The addition of anti-oxidant alloy elements is one of the strategies to improve the oxidation resistance of RHEAs, but it inevitably diminishes the mechanical properties.

causal_claim.content: Silicon diffusion and oxidation processes caused the silicide layer to move inward and thicken.
causal_claim.evidence_span: led to the increase of its thickness

causal_claim.content: Higher oxidation temperature increases the diffusion rate of silicon, leading to a deeper diffusion distance.
causal_claim.evidence_span: The coating oxidized at 1300 °C was thicker than the one oxidized at 1000 °C because of the higher diffusion rate of silicon, and the silicon had a deeper diffusion distance at the higher oxidation temperature

causal_claim.content: Continued silicon diffusion into the substrate during oxidation causes the high-silicon-content layer (L2) thickness to more than double.
causal_claim.evidence_span: Thus, during the oxidation process, silicon continued to diffuse into the substrate, and the thickness of the siliconized layer (L2) with a high silicon content are more than doubled.

causal_claim.content: Higher oxidation temperatures lead to more complete metal oxidation, resulting in a thicker oxide layer.
causal_claim.evidence_span: With the increasing temperature, the degree of oxidation of metal elements was more complete and the oxide layer became thicker

mechanism_principle.content: Volume expansion during oxidation causes the bulge phenomenon observed in the oxide layer.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: The swelling of the oxide layer may have been caused by volume expansion during oxidation.

mechanism_principle.content: Diffusion of silicon atoms into the substrate results in pore formation within the silicide layer.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: The pores formed in the silicide layer were resulted from the diffusion of a large number of silicon atoms into the RHEA substrate

mechanism_principle.content: The combination of complete metal/silicon oxidation increasing oxide volume and the volatilization of certain oxides reducing volume results in no net volume change, preventing cracks between layers at 1300 °C.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: The complete oxidation of the metal and silicon could cause a significant increase in the oxide layer volume, whereas the volatilization of some oxides (such as MoO 3 ) could cause the loss of the oxide layer and reduce the volume [ [34] ]. Consequently, the volume of the oxide layer was basically the same as that of the initial silicide layer. Therefore, no bulge phenomenon or cracks appeared between the oxide layer and the silicide layer.

hypothesis_statement.content: The authors propose to explore whether the Si-20Cr-20Fe coating can improve the oxidation resistance of MoNbTaTiW RHEA.
hypothesis_statement.evidence_span: The aim of this paper is to explore the feasibility of the Si-20Cr-20Fe coating in improving the oxidation resistance of MoNbTaTiW RHEA.

hypothesis_statement.content: The higher enthalpy of silicide formation for disilicides compared to other ratios leads to the stability of the disilicide surface layer.
hypothesis_statement.evidence_span: Samosonov et al. established the relationship between the enthalpies of silicide formation and the silicon content, suggesting that for each metal atom, the enthalpy of silicide formation increased with increasing silicon content. It indicated that the silicide tended to bind more silicon and disilicide had the best stability

evidence_result.content: The silicide coating is approximately 113 µm thick and exhibits a double-layer structure with varying silicon content.
evidence_result.evidence_span: It can be seen that the silicide coating was ~113 µm thick. According to the distribution of silicon content, the silicide coating had a double-layer structure: a thicker outer layer that contained a higher content of silicon and a thinner inner layer that had a lower content of silicon.
